mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to work and time
mcqs.question: A person lifts a 20 kg box through a height of 2 m in 4 s, while another person lifts the same box through the same height in 2 s. Which statement about their powers is correct?

options.A: Both have the same power because the work done is the same.
options.B: The person who lifts in 2 s has double the power of the other.
options.C: The person who lifts in 4 s has double the power of the other.
options.D: Power cannot be compared without knowing the force applied.

mcqs.answer: The person who lifts in 2 s has double the power of the other.
mcqs.explanation: Work done in both cases is mgh = 20 × 9.8 × 2 ≈ 392 J. Power = work/time. The first person: 392 J / 4 s = 98 W. The second person: 392 J / 2 s = 196 W, which is twice the first. Hence option B is correct; the others misinterpret the relationship.

mcqs.question: A 60 W bulb and a 100 W bulb are connected to the same 120 V supply. Which statement is true?

options.A: The 60 W bulb consumes more energy per hour than the 100 W bulb.
options.B: The 100 W bulb draws more current from the supply.
options.C: Both bulbs draw the same current because the voltage is the same.
options.D: The 60 W bulb has a higher resistance than the 100 W bulb.

mcqs.answer: The 100 W bulb draws more current from the supply.
mcqs.explanation: Power P = VI, so I = P/V. For the 60 W bulb, I = 60/120 = 0.5 A. For the 100 W bulb, I = 100/120 ≈ 0.83 A. Therefore the 100 W bulb draws more current. Option D is opposite (higher power means lower resistance). Options A and C are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines power in physics?

options.A: Power is the rate at which work is done.
options.B: Power is the total amount of work done.
options.C: Power is the force applied on an object.
options.D: Power is the distance moved per second.

mcqs.answer: Power is the rate at which work is done.
mcqs.explanation: Power measures how quickly work is performed or energy is transferred, expressed as P = work/time. Options B, C, and D describe work, force, and speed respectively, not power.

mcqs.question: A motor does 500 J of work in 25 s. What is its power?
mcqs.explanation: Power = work/time = 500 J / 25 s = 20 J/s = 20 W. The other options result from incorrect division.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand watt as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the watt?

options.A: Watt is the SI unit of energy.
options.B: Watt is the SI unit of power, equal to one joule per second.
options.C: Watt is the SI unit of force.
options.D: Watt is the SI unit of work.

mcqs.answer: Watt is the SI unit of power, equal to one joule per second.
mcqs.explanation: The watt (W) quantifies power, defined as one joule of energy transferred each second. Energy is measured in joules, not watts. Force is measured in newtons, and work shares the unit joule.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to work and time
mcqs.question: A water pump lifts water requiring 2000 J of work in 10 s. What is the power of the pump?
mcqs.explanation: Power = work/time = 2000 J / 10 s = 200 J/s = 200 W. The other options arise from misplaced decimal points or incorrect division.

mcqs.question: Which device will consume more electrical energy in 3 hours: a 1500 W heater or a 750 W fan?

options.A: The heater will consume more energy.
options.B: The fan will consume more energy.
options.C: Both will consume the same amount of energy.
options.D: Energy consumption cannot be determined without knowing the voltage.

mcqs.answer: The heater will consume more energy.
mcqs.explanation: Energy = power × time. For 3 h (10800 s), heater: 1500 W × 10800 s = 16.2 MJ. Fan: 750 W × 10800 s = 8.1 MJ. Higher power rating means higher energy use over the same period. Voltage is irrelevant for energy calculation when power is given.

mcqs.question: A cyclist climbs a hill, doing 3000 J of work in 150 s. How would you define the cyclist's power output?

options.A: Power is the total work done, which is 3000 J.
options.B: Power is the work done per unit time, which is 20 W.
options.C: Power is the time taken to do the work, which is 150 s.
options.D: Power is the force applied by the cyclist.

mcqs.answer: Power is the work done per unit time, which is 20 W.
mcqs.explanation: Power = work/time = 3000 J / 150 s = 20 J/s = 20 W. Option A confuses power with work, C confuses with time, and D confuses with force.
